correctness.rationale: The TRD characterization is proved directly from complete-multipartite adjacency: selected vertices must occupy at least two parts, and the complement must be empty or occupy at least two parts. This yields the singleton-coalition construction for every profile with at least three parts and order at least four and proves the star and triangle obstructions. Exhaustive direct adjacency and set-partition checks for all 58 multipartite profiles of orders 2 through 8 agree with the formula; those checks are corroborative, not the infinite proof.

evidence: Chellali et al. prove the maximum-value classification only in the triangle-free class; complete multipartite graphs with at least three parts contain triangles.
Their sufficient universal-vertex result requires minimum degree at least three and does not cover profiles such as \(K_{2,1,1}\), while the new theorem does.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The inspected general results do not dominate the multipartite claim: the triangle-free theorem is inapplicable and the universal-vertex sufficient condition is strictly narrower.

value.rationale: This is a complete exact classification on the canonical complete-multipartite family immediately extending the clique and biclique examples emphasized in the initiating paper. The at-least-three-part regime collapses to the maximum value with only the triangle exception, revealing a sharp structural transition rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
